mercy_translation.text:
When God, who has authority over all, made the human race through his own Word, he again saw the weakness of their nature: by itself it was not capable of knowing the Creator, nor even of forming a conception of God. For God is uncreated, while human beings were brought into being from nothing; God is incorporeal, while human beings were fashioned below in a body; and in general there is a great deficiency in created things when it comes to comprehending and knowing the One who made them. Therefore, again having mercy on the human race—for he is good—he did not leave them without knowledge of himself, lest even their existence become useless to them.

For what benefit is there to creatures if they do not know their own Maker? And how could they be rational if they did not know the Word of the Father, through whom they themselves came to be? They would differ in nothing from irrational creatures if they knew nothing beyond earthly things. And why would God have made those by whom he did not wish to be known?

Therefore, so that this would not happen, being good he shared with them his own Image, our Lord Jesus Christ, and made them according to his image and likeness. Through such grace, by contemplating the Image—that is, the Word of the Father—they could form a conception of the Father himself, and by knowing their Maker live the truly blessed and happy life.

But human beings, once again becoming foolish, neglected even the grace given to them. They turned so far away from God and darkened their souls so deeply that they not only forgot the knowledge of God but fashioned one thing after another for themselves in his place. They formed idols for themselves instead of the truth and preferred things that do not exist to the God who truly is, worshiping creation rather than the Creator. Worst of all, they transferred the honor due to God to wood, stones, every kind of material thing, and even to human beings, doing still more than these things, as was said earlier.

So far did they fall into impiety that they even worshiped demons and proclaimed them gods, satisfying their desires. They offered sacrifices of irrational animals and, as was said before, even slaughtered human beings as offerings due to them, binding themselves ever more tightly to the frenzy of those powers.

For this reason magical practices were taught among them, oracles in various places deceived people, and everyone attributed the causes of their birth and existence to the stars and to the things in heaven, thinking of nothing beyond what is visible.

In short, everything was full of impiety and lawlessness. God alone and his Word were not known, although he had not hidden himself invisibly from human beings nor given them only one simple way of knowing him. Rather, he had spread abroad the knowledge of himself for them in many different ways and through many means.

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
Athanasius develops the epistemological problem of fallen humanity: the image was given so that the Father might be known through the Word.
The chapter distinguishes the uncreated God from created humanity and links idolatry to loss of the knowledge of God.
